title: Sulfurization run (lab draft)
summary: Sulfurization–annealing of FIB-irradiated MoSe₂ combining the lab's furnace notes with the published sequence; the published program and the local recipe are listed separately because they are different experiments. Unspecified operating settings must come from the lab's furnace procedure.

steps.title: Identify the sample and intended experiment
steps.body: Record the sample ID, substrate, and whether the MoSe₂ has undergone focused-ion-beam irradiation. The paper's selective-conversion process uses irradiated MoSe₂ monolayers on SiO₂/Si.

steps.title: Complete irradiation for the paper's selective process
steps.body: Complete the ion irradiation if reproducing the paper's selective process. The authors used Ga⁺ ions at 5 kV, with beam currents of 5, 20, or 80 pA. Select the dose and pattern corresponding to the result being reproduced; these currents are reported alternatives, not consecutive steps. Record the irradiation parameters and retain an unirradiated reference region.

steps.title: Prepare the cooling system
steps.body: Following your local setup, prepare ice for the intended cooling-water reservoir and establish cooling according to the equipment procedure. Confirm that cooling operates before starting the furnace.

steps.title: Check the argon supply
steps.body: Your notes specify a reading above 5 psi. Confirm which gauge this refers to and use the approved supply setting. Do not interpret this value as a tube-pressure target. The paper does not specify this pressure threshold.
steps.caution: Do not interpret this value as a tube-pressure target. The paper does not specify this pressure threshold.

steps.title: Inspect the tube and connections
steps.body: Check the quartz tube, seals, sample support, thermocouple, vacuum connection, argon inlet, and exhaust connection to the fume hood. Confirm the valve identities before operating them.

steps.title: Perform any required preliminary empty-tube purge
steps.body: Your notes describe three evacuation–argon exchange cycles using the vacuum connection on the left. This is a preliminary atmosphere exchange, not a substitute for removing physical residue or for purging after loading.
steps.check: Preliminary purge complete: three exchange cycles

steps.title: Prepare to open the sample assembly
steps.body: With the furnace cool, isolate the connections and equalize pressure according to the equipment procedure. Remove the thermocouple if necessary to withdraw the sample-support assembly toward the right, as you described.

steps.title: Load the sulfur and sample
steps.body: Place sulfur in a quartz boat or crucible and position the sample chip beside the sulfur container. Your proposed sulfur quantity is 1–2 g, but the paper does not report a mass. Its supporting methods place the sulfur crucible and sample next to each other on a silicon-carbide stage.
steps.caution: The sample chip goes beside the sulfur container, not on it; no other sample placement is reported. The paper does not report a sulfur mass.

steps.title: Reassemble the furnace
steps.body: Return the sample assembly to its defined position, reinstall the thermocouple, and seal the tube. Record the positions of the sample, sulfur boat, and thermocouple.

steps.title: Purge after loading and resealing
steps.body: Opening the tube introduces air, so the preliminary purge does not establish the final processing atmosphere. Your described exchange sequence is: evacuate the tube; isolate the vacuum line; admit argon to the approved backfill condition; isolate the argon supply; evacuate again and repeat the exchange until the required three cycles are completed. The vacuum endpoint, backfill pressure, final atmosphere, and exact cycle-counting convention require the local procedure. You described closing the fume-hood outlet during the exchanges; confirm that valve arrangement against the actual plumbing. This does not mean the tube should remain sealed during heating.
steps.caution: Closing the fume-hood outlet during the exchanges must be confirmed against the actual plumbing. This does not mean the tube should remain sealed during heating.
steps.check: Post-loading purge complete and the valve arrangement confirmed

steps.title: Close the furnace cover and select recipe
steps.body: Close the furnace cover and select the temperature recipe. The paper used infrared heating of a silicon-carbide stage. Your clamshell furnace uses a different arrangement, so confirm how its thermocouple reading relates to the sample temperature.

steps.title: Perform published sulfurization at 700 °C
steps.body: For the published process, heat the sample in the presence of sulfur to 700 °C and hold for approximately 10 minutes. The publication does not specify a numerical heating ramp rate.

steps.title: Remove sulfur vapor before the higher-temperature anneal
steps.body: Flush the chamber with a steady argon flow to deplete sulfur vapor. The publication does not specify a flow rate, flushing duration, or endpoint; those must be established for your apparatus.

steps.title: Perform the published annealing step
steps.body: After sulfur depletion, increase the temperature to approximately 900 °C and hold for approximately 5 minutes. This stage promotes structural recovery while limiting sulfur incorporation into unirradiated regions.

steps.title: Alternative: run the local 900 °C recipe
steps.body: This step substitutes for Steps 12–14 if intentionally testing your local recipe. Your proposed program is: 20 °C/min ramp to 900 °C (≈44 min from 20 °C); 30 min hold at 900 °C; non-flowing argon for the first 20 min, using the confirmed pressure-management arrangement; argon flow to the fume hood for the final 10 min through the approved exhaust route. This is a modified recipe, not the paper's published sequence. Sulfur remains present during a much longer high-temperature treatment, which can affect unirradiated MoSe₂ as well as irradiated regions.
steps.caution: This is a modified recipe, not the paper's published sequence. Sulfur remains present during a much longer high-temperature treatment, which can affect unirradiated MoSe₂ as well as irradiated regions.

steps.title: Cool the sample
steps.body: The paper states that samples were cooled to room temperature without specifying a rate. Your local recipe requests 20 °C/min to room temperature. Confirm that the furnace can achieve this rate, record the actual temperature trace, and use the lab-defined gas conditions throughout cooling.
steps.caution: The furnace's ability to achieve the 20 °C/min cooling rate must be confirmed.

steps.title: Unload the sample
steps.body: Once the apparatus has reached the required unloading temperature, establish the appropriate pressure condition, open the assembly, and retrieve the chip according to the equipment procedure.
steps.check: Unloading temperature and pressure condition reached

steps.title: Characterize and document the result
steps.body: Compare optical images, Raman spectra, and photoluminescence from processed and reference regions. The authors used 532 nm excitation, a 100× objective, an ≈1 µm spot, and laser power below 100 µW. Record the sulfur mass, sample positions, irradiation dose, actual temperature history, gas conditions, and every deviation from the published method. Details: Supporting Information pp. 2–3 and Figure S1 (acs.figshare.com, article 29318379).
